capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- For the first statement, use the Dirichlet-convolution identity
  \[
  \mu * \log=-\Lambda.
  \]
  Evaluating this arithmetic-function identity at \(n\) unfolds convolution as
  \[
  \sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\log d=-\Lambda(n).
  \]
  The \(n=0\) case is absorbed by the library definitions: `Nat.divisors 0` is empty and `vonMangoldt 0 = 0`. The remaining work is only normalization of the cast \(\mathbb Z\to\mathbb R\).

- For the second statement, invoke the Dirichlet-series representation of the Riemann zeta function on its half-plane of absolute convergence:
  \[
  \zeta(s)=\sum_{n\ge 1}\frac1{n^s},\qquad \Re(s)>1.
  \]
  Match this with the displayed `tsum` over `Nat`; its \(n=0\) term is zero under the complex-power/division conventions, so it is the same positive-integer series. Absolute convergence from `1 < s.re` justifies the unconditional summation and any required reindexing.

Thus the useful intermediate goals are the evaluated Möbius–log convolution identity and the standard zeta Dirichlet-series theorem, followed by definitional simplification.
